title: Scar Tissue

beats.what: Tabitha and Boyd argue in the night after she returned; fight escalates to divorce being named out loud for the first time
Julie hears the fight and confronts Tabitha; says she is glad things are getting back to normal, dripping with irony
Jade explains dimensional rift theory to Tabitha; she cuts him off, wants to see what he actually found
Victor invites his newly-found father Henry to walk with him toward the tunnels; warns it is dangerous
Boyd learns the ambulance carried a portable ultrasound; tells Henry to tell Fatima to come by, quietly asks Henry not to mention Boyd came
Tabitha reveals to Jade at the bottle tree that as a little girl she had the same recurring nightmare of this place, just like Miranda

character_beats.beat: wants validation that going through the Farway tree was worth it; instead finds everyone including Boyd believes she failed them -- and she cannot stop agreeing with them
keeps his distance from the Fatima pregnancy crisis all episode, deflecting to logistics; his offer to cover the ultrasound visit is the closest he gets to confronting it
throws himself into bottle-number theory as substitute for sobriety; ghost of dead Tom appears and calls out his avoidance

key_lines.line: I should've done more. When I was out there, I should've done more.
key_lines.why: Tabitha's guilt sets the episode's emotional spine

key_lines.line: You had an opportunity none of us have ever had, and you blew it.
key_lines.why: Community's verdict on her return lands here

key_lines.line: I don't want to. I have to. It's going to save them.
key_lines.why: Victor's contradiction in miniature: duty vs. dread

key_lines.line: I want you to be honest!
key_lines.why: Tabitha names what the whole marriage is fighting about

key_lines.line: It wasn't just Miranda. I saw this place too.
key_lines.why: Episode-closing revelation plants the season's central mystery

open_loops: Why did Tabitha dream of this place as a child, like Miranda did -- and what does that mean about her role here?
What is the significance of the numbers in the bottle-tree bottles, and what pattern do 'backwards 2' and 'backwards 7' signal?
Victor is descending into the tunnels to find Jasper; what secret did Jasper once tell Christopher?
Fatima is experiencing something invisible to the ultrasound -- is it supernatural or psychosomatic?

payoffs.what: Jade's weeks of studying bottle-tree bottles converge with Tabitha's childhood nightmare -- both are now pointed at the same mystery
Tabitha's escape through the Farway tree is replayed in recap and then interrogated by the whole town in the meeting

contradiction.wants: to be seen as someone who did everything possible when she was out there
contradiction.does: admits to Boyd, to Donna, and finally to herself that she should have done more -- every conversation confirms the failure she cannot accept

tone_notes: Density spikes at minutes 4-5 (197 wpm) and 33-34 (149 wpm) map to the night-fight and the bottle-tree confrontation with Tom's ghost respectively. The episode's longest silence -- 52 seconds from 06:47 to 07:38 -- lands between the fight and Julie's morning confrontation, giving the damage time to settle. The overall pace (78.5 wpm) is the slowest in the batch, matching the episode's emotional paralysis: everyone is processing rather than acting.
